rows.answer: GraphRAG answers global questions about a whole corpus by using map-reduce processing of community summaries [S1]. These summaries are generated in a bottom-up manner following the hierarchical structure of extracted communities, with higher-level summaries recursively incorporating lower-level summaries [S1]. Finally, the partial answers from the map step are combined in the reduce step to generate a global answer [S1].

rows.answer: Late chunking is a strategy that leverages the difference in size between the long context input windows of recent embedding models and the relatively small size of optimal text chunks for most applications [S3]. It involves encoding text in a way that allows the model to capture context before chunking the text, enabling it to handle longer input sequences [S2]. This approach requires no additional training and can be implemented in any long-context text embedding model that uses mean pooling with any chunking technique [S2].
